findings.gap: Protocol failures are not retained after a pending request resolves. A prohibited server request arriving immediately after the final command response can trigger finish(), yet a subsequent graceful child exit still permits a passed receipt with protocolError set to false.
findings.risk: A protocol-invalid execution can supply passing native-isolation evidence. The in-memory reproduction retained the successful command response and accepted terminal exit 0 after rejecting an unsolicited server request.
findings.spec_ref: Local candidate delta, Review, evidence and delivery: usable transport, no unsupported isolation claim, and preservation of completed-but-invalid execution facts; architecture-guidelines item 4.

findings.gap: RPC input failures can escape the asynchronous failure handler: child.stdin has no error listener, and receive() accesses value.method without checking whether parsed JSON is null. Both EPIPE and a null protocol frame throw outside the awaited request.
findings.risk: An initialization pipe failure or malformed response can terminate the preflight without its structured unavailable result or bounded child cleanup. In-memory reproductions left the request pending and invoked no child termination.
findings.spec_ref: Local candidate delta, Review, evidence and delivery: preserve initialization stdin and terminate the child within the declared bound; architecture-guidelines item 4.
